heuristics: Canonicalized parallel rho walk modeled as a uniform random function on an m=r/6-element set; empirically measured success rate (47-55%) at the exact claimed budget supports this beyond the toy-scale assumption alone.
Mod-r multiplication reuses the pinned mod-p instruction count as a same-bit-length analogy (the Frobenius-power cost itself, 11 Fp mults, is independently derived, not an analogy).
The chaining table's O(1)-expected traversal cost is a standard balls-into-bins linearity-of-expectation argument.
The 2% escape-rate bound is empirically supported (measured ~0.4% at L=32 matching production), not a proven worst case.
limitations: Analytic construction; no full-size execution. experiment.py exercises the exact production mechanism (including matching L=32 and the exact birthday-scale budget) on a toy exponent group, not production field/pairing arithmetic.

Does not attempt a SexTNFS-based score: literature estimates for BLS12-381 GT security under STNFS cluster 117-133 bits, but no source gives a reviewable instruction-level cost comparable in rigor to this ledger.
Does not use Satoh's Miller Inversion; a prior revision showed it cost-equivalent to the simpler scalar multiplication used here.
